extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and scholars interested in Joseph Heller's Catch-22 and literary analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts criteria and features used to evaluate or describe the novel Catch-22 (narrative techniques, themes, motifs, characterisation, tone, and structural devices). Useful for literary analysis or informing creative-writing choices imitating Heller's approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-chronological third-person omniscient narration
rubrics_metrics.description: uses a distinctive non-chronological third-person omniscient narration, describing events from the points of view of different characters; the separate storylines are out of sequence so the timeline develops along with the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The novel's timeline is deliberately shuffled: events occur out of order and the reader must piece together the chronology as new viewpoint information appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple points of view and repeated descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many events in the book are repeatedly described from differing points of view, so the reader learns more about each event from each iteration, with the new information often completing a joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisiting the same events from different characters' vantage points adds layers of information and comedic effect; repetition is a structural device rather than redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent repetition of words, phrases, and questions for comic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific words, phrases, and questions are also repeated frequently, generally to comic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated motifs/phrases should be used to build jokes, echoes, and thematic resonance across the novel rather than incidental reiteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular and repetitive prose exemplifying Catch-22 structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of Heller's prose in Catch-22 is circular and repetitive, exemplifying in its form the structure of a Catch-22. Circular reasoning is widely used by some characters to justify their actions and opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of circular logic and self-referential arguments can mirror thematic absurdity; characters may be shown using paradoxical rationales to justify decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free-association based structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Although its nonchronological structure may at first seem random, Catch-22 is highly structured. It is founded on a structure of free association; ideas run into one another through seemingly random connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect scenes and chapters via associative links (objects, minor characters, phrases) so transitions feel organic even when non-linear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episodic chapters with thematically unique focus
rubrics_metrics.description: As Heller utilizes an episodic structure for most of the novel, many chapters may appear to be a disjointed series of events with little or no connection with each other. However, individual chapters often deal with thematically unique ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat chapters as self-contained thematic vignettes that nevertheless contribute to larger motifs and character arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-focused chapters and extensive cast development
rubrics_metrics.description: While a few characters are most prominent, especially Yossarian and the Chaplain, the majority of named characters are described in detail with fleshed out or multidimensional personas to the extent that there are few if any 'minor characters'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide developed, multidimensional portrayals for many characters rather than relegating most to flat 'minor' roles; consider titular chapters for character exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aversion to traditional heroes (antiheroic perspective)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no traditional heroes in the novel, reflecting the underlying commentary that war has no heroes, only victims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize flawed, contradictory protagonists (antiheroes) whose moral character may develop over the narrative rather than depicting idealized heroes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paradox as central thematic device
rubrics_metrics.description: Paradox — exemplified by the Catch-22 rule itself and characters' reasoning — pervades the book; the narrator revels in paradoxical situations and logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed paradoxical dilemmas that trap characters in no-win situations; make the logic internally consistent yet absurd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire of military bureaucracy and greed (bureaucratic absurdity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel satirizes military bureaucracy and greed. The motif of bureaucratic absurdity is one of the book's primary motifs, including rules that justify otherwise arbitrary actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray institutions using specious legalistic justification and procedures that produce absurd or harmful outcomes; use bureaucracy as a source of dark comedy and critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragedy and farce interplay (miscommunication leading to tragedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of the farce in the novel is fueled by intentional and unintentional miscommunication, occasionally leading to tragic consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance comic miscommunication with the possibility of real harm; allow farce to escalate into genuine tragedy to underscore moral weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodicy and existential questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Theodicy is a theme: Yossarian questions the idea that God is all-powerful, all-good, and all-knowing; the narrator often treats God as incompetent or uncaring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characters' philosophical or theological reflections to deepen existential themes and question larger moral orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military–industrial complex and profit-driven violence
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel emphasizes the danger of profit-seeking by portraying Milo's syndicate and the military–industrial complex; violence is sometimes generated as a means to profit rather than ideological ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict economic motives and corporate-like logic within wartime settings to critique depersonalized profit-driven violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catch-22 as conceptual device (no-win rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Catch-22' is 'a problem for which the only solution is denied by a circumstance inherent in the problem or by a rule'. In the book, Catch-22 functions as a military rule typifying bureaucratic operation and reasoning; because it does not exist in a repealable sense, it exerts potent effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce formally specified paradoxical rules or axioms that trap characters, and use them as recurring motifs to illuminate institutional absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of anachronism to situate contemporary critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Heller intentionally included anachronisms (e.g., loyalty oaths, IBM machines) though the novel is set in World War II, to situate the book in the context of the 1950s and comment on contemporary issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate anachronisms may be employed to draw parallels between the story's nominal historical setting and later/other political contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonal shift toward darker realism/horror in later sections
rubrics_metrics.description: For most of the book, the reader is cushioned from the full horror of war, but the final section lays bare horrors (e.g., pointless attack, rape and murder), the sixth part takes a much darker turn and emphasizes the darkness and brutality of war and life in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow tone to shift over the course of the work: sustained comic or absurd material can give way to stark, horrific scenes to alter reader perception and moral stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative revelation and delayed disclosure (narrative withholding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key facts (e.g., the full details of Snowden's death) are revealed later in the book after iterative references, creating cumulative impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use delayed disclosure and iterative foreshadowing so that repeated allusions culminate in meaningful revelations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of titled chapters centering on characters or concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Many chapters are titled by characters (e.g., 'The Texan', 'Clevinger') and focus on that person's perspective or thematic idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider structuring chapters around individual characters or concepts to foreground particular viewpoints and themes.
